title: Orbit Kummer field and its equivariant normal relative model
statement:
Let $k$ be a field, $S$ a normal integral projective finite-type $k$-scheme, $K=k(S)$, and $f:X\to S$ an H-projective morphism with $X$ integral of finite type over $k$. Assume all geometric fibres of $f$ are pure of dimension one and $C=X_K$ is smooth and geometrically integral. Put $F=k(X)$. Assume also that $X$ is normal. Let a finite group $G$ act compatibly on $k,X,S,f$, and let $M\subset C$ be a reduced finite etale closed subscheme stable under $G$. Fix a prime $\ell\geq5$ different from $\operatorname{char}k$ and assume $K$ contains a primitive $\ell$th root of unity. Let $S=\bigcup_iU_i$ be a finite affine cover by nonempty opens and $\varphi_i:X_{U_i}\to\mathbf P^1_{U_i}$ finite surjective morphisms whose generic fibres are generically etale, with reduced finite etale inverse images of $0,1,\infty$ disjoint from $M$. Write $x_i\in F$ for their affine coordinate functions and, in an algebraic closure of $F$, put
$$L=F\bigl(\sqrt[\ell]{g(x_i)},\sqrt[\ell]{g(x_i-1)}:i,\ g\in G\bigr),\quad B_0=F^G,\quad E=\{z\in L:z\text{ is algebraic over }K\}.$$
Every function in this root list is nonzero. The reduced union $D\subset C$ of all $G$-translates of the three special inverse images is finite etale, disjoint from $M$, and contains the zeros and poles of every function in the list. The extensions $L/B_0$ and $L/F$ are finite Galois and $E/K$ is finite separable. The normalization of $C$ in $L$ is smooth over $K$, etale away from $D$, and, with its induced $E$-structure, is a smooth projective geometrically integral $E$-curve. Inside $L$ one has $E\cap F=K$. Define
$$J=\{(g,\tau)\in G\times\operatorname{Aut}_{B_0}(L):\tau|_F=g|_F\},\qquad N=\ker(J\to G).$$
The projection $J\to G$ is surjective, $N=\operatorname{Aut}_F(L)$, and $L^N=F$. The group $J$ preserves $E$ and $E^N=K$. Put $T=\operatorname{Nor}_E(S)$ and $Y=\operatorname{Nor}_L(X)$. Then $T$ is normal integral projective of finite type over $k$, $Y$ is normal integral of finite type over $k$, and $T\to S$ and $Y\to X\times_ST$ are finite surjective. The morphism $Y\to T$ is H-projective with pure one-dimensional geometric fibres and the stated smooth geometrically integral generic curve. The group $J$ acts compatibly on this diagram, lifting the $G$-actions. The reduced generic inverse image of $M$ is finite etale over $E$ and stable under $J$. These conclusions allow nonfaithful semilinear actions.

Normal means that every local ring is an integrally closed domain. H-projective means admitting a closed immersion into a finite-dimensional projective space over the target. A finite separable field extension is finite-dimensional with separable minimal polynomials. A finite Galois extension is a finite normal separable extension; normal for fields means that every irreducible polynomial over the smaller field with a root in the larger field splits there. For a group $G$ acting on a field $V$, $V^G$ is the subfield of elements fixed by every member of $G$. All fixed-field equalities below use the field embeddings induced by the displayed scheme maps. A primitive $\ell$th root of unity is an element of multiplicative order $\ell$. A finite morphism of integral curves is generically etale when it is etale over a dense open subset of its target. The notions used are [def-weil-field], [def-pc-integral-scheme], [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], [def-kun-projective], [def-sc-function-field], [def-pc-field-extension], [def-weil-pure-dimension], [def-weil-geometric-fibre], [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible], [def-fin-normalization-extension], [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], [def-weil-surjective-morphism], [def-pc-fibre-product], [def-weil-etale-morphism], [def-nagata-projective-space-base-change], [def-pc-genus], [def-weil-algebraic-closure].

proof.text: Base change the projective morphism to $\operatorname{Spec}K$. Thus $C$ is projective, and its assumed smoothness, geometric integrality and dimension make it a smooth projective integral curve. Each generic pencil is surjective, so $x_i$ is nonconstant and $x_i,x_i-1$ are nonzero. Automorphisms preserve nonzero elements. The zeros and poles of $x_i$ lie over $0,\infty$ and those of $x_i-1$ over $1,\infty$. The same assertion after $g$ places every translated divisor in the indicated union $D$. A reduced finite etale scheme over a field is a finite disjoint union of spectra of finite separable residue fields. The reduced union of these translated point sets therefore has this form as well and is finite etale. Semilinear translation changes the base by a field isomorphism and preserves separability. Since $M$ is stable and each original point set avoids it, so does $D$. In particular every root-list function and its inverse is regular on $C\setminus D$.

source.place: §§3.4--3.5, pp.606--607; reduced special fibres and their finite orbit union

proof.text: Let $A$ be the finite list of translated functions, of length $r$. A primitive $\ell$th root $\zeta\in K$ gives all roots $1,\zeta,\ldots,\zeta^{\ell-1}$ of $T^\ell-1$ in $F$: they are distinct and account for its degree. Apply the multiradical lemma with $n=\ell$. It gives finite Galois $L/F$ and $d=[L:F]\mid\ell^r$. In particular $d$ is invertible in $K$. Apply radical normalization with $U=C\setminus D$ to get a normal integral projective $K$-curve $\widetilde C$, finite surjective over $C$, etale over $U$, and with specified function field $L$. Apply tame Galois curve normalization: its hypotheses are exactly the smoothness of $C$, the finite Galois extension of invertible degree $d$, the reduced finite etale $D$, and the etaleness over $U$ just obtained. Hence $\widetilde C$ is smooth over $K$.

source.place: §3.5, p.607; Stacks Fields 09I6 section-Kummer and tame residue argument 09EB, 0B8Y

proof.text: Apply the smooth-cover constant-field marking lemma to $\widetilde C\to C$, the open $U=C\setminus D$, and $M\subset U$. It identifies the algebraic constants in $L$ with $E=\Gamma(\widetilde C,\mathcal O)$, proves $E/K$ finite separable, and supplies the canonical $E$-structure. Over $E$ the curve is smooth projective geometrically integral with function field $L$, and $\widetilde C\times_C M$ is reduced finite etale over $E$. It also gives $E\cap F=K$. This uses the actual finite cover and its etale locus, rather than inferring smoothness from normality over a possibly imperfect field.

Apply the finite faithful action theorem to the image $H$ of $G\to\operatorname{Aut}(F)$. Its fixed field is $B_0$, so $F/B_0$ is finite Galois; choose a primitive element $b$ for this finite separable extension. The polynomial $P(T)=\prod_{h\in H}(T-h(b))\prod_{a\in A}(T^\ell-a)$ has coefficients in $B_0$: $H$ permutes the first factors and $G$ permutes the root list in the second product. It splits over $L$, since every root of $T^\ell-a$ is a chosen radical multiplied by a power of $\zeta$. Its roots generate $L$ over $B_0$, because they include $b$ and all chosen radicals. The splitting-field theorem therefore makes $L/B_0$ finite and normal. Separability follows from $F/B_0$, $L/F$ and separable transitivity. Thus $L/B_0$ is finite Galois. Repeated factors in $P$ cause no problem: its separability is not asserted or used.

source.place: §3.5, p.607, invariance of the radical field; Stacks 09I3, 030N, 09HB

proof.text: For $g\in G$, its restriction to $F$ fixes $B_0$. The normal intermediate-isomorphism lifting theorem extends it to an automorphism $\tau$ of $L/B_0$. Thus $(g,\tau)\in J$ and $J\to G$ is onto. Composition and inversion preserve the defining restriction condition, so $J$ is a subgroup of $G\times\operatorname{Aut}_{B_0}(L)$; it is finite by finite Galois theory. Its kernel is exactly the pairs $(1,\tau)$ with $\tau|_F=1$, giving $N=\operatorname{Aut}_F(L)$. Finite Galois theory gives $L^N=F$. Each $\tau$ sends $K$ to $K$, hence preserves the set $E$ of elements algebraic over $K$. Consequently $E^N=E\cap L^N=E\cap F=K$. This identifies the kernel using the fibre-product group even when the original $G$-action has a kernel.

source.place: §3.5, p.607, fibre-product lifting group; Stacks 0BME (2), 09I1 and 09DW

proof.text: The composite $X\to S\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is H-projective by composition. Apply the semilinear finite normalization model first to $S$, the extension $E/K$, and the $J$-action just constructed, and then to $X$, the extension $L/F$, and the action of $J$ on $X$ through $G$. This gives the specified models $T=\operatorname{Nor}_E(S)$ and $Y=\operatorname{Nor}_L(X)$, their canonical generic identifications, normality, integrality, projectivity and finite type over $k$, and finite surjective maps $T\to S$, $Y\to X$. It also gives actions with field action exactly the prescribed $J$-actions and compatible with their action on $k$.

The generic maps give $\operatorname{Spec}L\to X\times_ST$, and the latter scheme is integral over $X$ because $T\to S$ is finite. Apply the relative-normalization universal property for $\operatorname{Spec}L\to X$ to obtain $h:Y\to X\times_ST$ and hence $g:Y\to T$. This is the normalization used here: its affine ring is the integral closure in $L$. The uniqueness clause makes both maps $J$-equivariant, since their conjugates agree on $\operatorname{Spec}L$. The map $h$ is finite. Indeed over $\operatorname{Spec}R\subset X$ the product is $\operatorname{Spec}B$ for a finite $R$-algebra $B$, and $Y$ is $\operatorname{Spec}C$ for a finite $R$-algebra $C$. The factorization gives $B\to C$, and any finite set of $R$-module generators of $C$ also generates it over $B$.

source.place: §3.5, pp.607--608; Stacks 035H and 035I, normalization factorization; affine module calculation

proof.text: We check surjectivity onto the full product $Z=X\times_ST$. The finite dominant map $T\to S$ is universally open since $S$ is normal and locally Noetherian. Hence $Z\to X$ is open. Both schemes are Noetherian of finite type over $k$, so $Z$ has finitely many irreducible components. Each component has a nonempty open part avoiding the other components. Its image is nonempty open in integral $X$ and contains the generic point $\eta_X$. Thus every component of $Z$ meets $Z_{\eta_X}$. This fibre is $\operatorname{Spec}(F\otimes_K E)$. It is integral: choose a nonempty affine $\operatorname{Spec}R\subset C$; geometric integrality says $R\otimes_K E$ is a domain, and localization gives $F\otimes_K E$. It is a field since finite-dimensional over $F$. Thus $Z_{\eta_X}$ has one point. The unique point of this fibre belongs to every chosen open part avoiding the other components. If two components existed, the open part for the first would exclude the point that belongs to the second. Thus there is exactly one component and $Z$ is irreducible. The finite map $h$ has closed image and contains this point (the map from $\operatorname{Spec}L$), hence is surjective.

source.place: §3.5, pp.607--608, full base-change image; normal-base openness and elementary component argument

proof.text: Integral closure commutes with localization. Localizing the affine charts of $Y\to X$ along nonzero elements of the base therefore identifies $Y\times_S\operatorname{Spec}K$ with the normalization $\widetilde C$ of $C$ in $L$. The same chart calculation identifies $T\times_S\operatorname{Spec}K$ with $\operatorname{Spec}E$. Hence $Y\times_T\operatorname{Spec}E=\widetilde C$, with the canonical $E$-structure from its inclusion into $L$. This generic fibre is nonempty and pure of dimension one, smooth projective and geometrically integral by step 3. In particular $g$ is dominant. Apply the finite-curve-factor lemma to $q:T\to S$, $\nu:Y\to X$, $g$ and the finite map $h$. All four schemes are integral finite type, $f$ and $S/k$ are H-projective, $q,\nu$ are finite surjective, and the required generic curve has just been identified. It gives H-projectivity of $g$ and pure one-dimensional geometric fibres.

source.place: §3.5, pp.607--608; Stacks 0307, 01WE, 02FZ, 02FY, and the finite-curve-factor dimension bounds

proof.text: Under the generic-fibre identification of step 9, the reduced generic inverse image of $M$ is exactly $\widetilde C\times_C M$. Step 3 made it reduced finite etale over $E$. The $J$-equivariance of the diagram and the $G$-stability of $M$ make this inverse image stable under $J$. The projection to $G$ is the one already shown surjective, so the diagram lifts the original actions. No step identified $G$ with its automorphism image: the image $H$ was used only to apply the faithful fixed-field theorem, and the actual lifting group remains the fibre product $J$. Thus all conclusions also hold for nonfaithful semilinear actions.

Shape is fine: one commit, no new nodes, and the statement is identical to live. Live and side-live still have the item unsplit, so no supersession. proof_deps equals the union of the step uses, and nothing is cited from SGA. All 10 steps check. Step 1: the pencils are finite surjective, so x_i and x_i-1 are nonzero, and D, the union of the semilinear translates, is finite étale by 02GL plus the coproduct lemma; it avoids M because M is G-stable. Step 2: the multiradical lemma gives L/F Galois of degree dividing ell^r, radical normalization with U=C\D gives the model, and the tame lemma gives smoothness without a regular-implies-smooth step over imperfect K. Step 3: the marking-lemma hypotheses hold (M lies in U because D and M are disjoint) and give E, E/K finite separable and E∩F=K. Step 4: the orbit polynomial is invariant because G permutes the (i,g)-indexed list; it splits in L and generates L, so the splitting-field node and separable permanence make L/B0 Galois. Step 5: 0BME(2) at F gives J onto G, N=Aut_F(L) and L^N=F; τ preserves K and hence E, so E^N=K. Step 6: 01WE plus the semilinear model with σ=τ|_E and σ=τ, using the inverse-pullback convention throughout. Step 7: the universal property plus uniqueness for the affine map Z→X gives h and its equivariance; h is finite by the generator argument. Step 8: universal openness, finitely many components, and the generic fibre Spec(F⊗_K E) being a field (geometric integrality, localization) make Z irreducible, and the closed image of h is all of Z. The implicit point that z is the generic point is one line. Step 9: localizing the integral closure (0307) gives Y_K = C̃ and T_K = Spec E, and the finite-curve-factor hypotheses all hold. Step 10 is elementary. Edge cases: nonfaithful G, degree one, empty M, zero-dimensional S, imperfect K. Batch 5: lem-trf-h-projective-composition is Stacks 01WE; its closure has no other trf or pod node, so it is generic and accepted. lem-sfb-finite-curve-factor-projective-pure reaches trf only through Proj and projective-bundle geometry (projective-bundle-to-h-projective, proj-separated, line-proj charts, algebraic-space definitions, pod separated base change); this is generic and not part of the trace-formula or Poincaré-duality proofs, so it is accepted. The four tool_uses (01WF, 02GL, étale coproduct, 01WE) are generic and accepted. statement_change.old_statement:
Let $k$ be a field, $S$ a normal integral projective finite-type $k$-scheme, $K=k(S)$, and $f:X\to S$ an H-projective morphism with $X$ integral of finite type over $k$. Assume all geometric fibres of $f$ are pure of dimension one and $C=X_K$ is smooth and geometrically integral. Put $F=k(X)$. Assume also that $X$ is normal. Let a finite group $G$ act compatibly on $k,X,S,f$, and let $M\subset C$ be a reduced finite etale closed subscheme stable under $G$. Fix a prime $\ell\geq5$ different from $\operatorname{char}k$ and assume $K$ contains a primitive $\ell$th root of unity. Let $S=\bigcup_iU_i$ be a finite affine cover and $\varphi_i:X_{U_i}\to\mathbf P^1_{U_i}$ finite surjective morphisms whose generic fibres are generically etale, with reduced finite etale inverse images of $0,1,\infty$ disjoint from $M$. Write $x_i\in F$ for their affine coordinate functions and, in an algebraic closure of $F$, put
$$L=F\bigl(\sqrt[\ell]{g(x_i)},\sqrt[\ell]{g(x_i-1)}:i,\ g\in G\bigr),\quad B_0=F^G,\quad E=\{z\in L:z\text{ is algebraic over }K\}.$$
Every function in this root list is nonzero. The reduced union $D\subset C$ of all $G$-translates of the three special inverse images is finite etale, disjoint from $M$, and contains the zeros and poles of every function in the list. The extensions $L/B_0$ and $L/F$ are finite Galois and $E/K$ is finite separable. The normalization of $C$ in $L$ is smooth over $K$, etale away from $D$, and, with its induced $E$-structure, is a smooth projective geometrically integral $E$-curve. Inside $L$ one has $E\cap F=K$. Define
$$J=\{(g,\tau)\in G\times\operatorname{Aut}_{B_0}(L):\tau|_F=g|_F\},\qquad N=\ker(J\to G).$$
The projection $J\to G$ is surjective, $N=\operatorname{Aut}_F(L)$, and $L^N=F$. The group $J$ preserves $E$ and $E^N=K$. Put $T=\operatorname{Nor}_E(S)$ and $Y=\operatorname{Nor}_L(X)$. Then $T$ is normal integral projective of finite type over $k$, $Y$ is normal integral of finite type over $k$, and $T\to S$ and $Y\to X\times_ST$ are finite surjective. The morphism $Y\to T$ is H-projective with pure one-dimensional geometric fibres and the stated smooth geometrically integral generic curve. The group $J$ acts compatibly on this diagram, lifting the $G$-actions. The reduced generic inverse image of $M$ is finite etale over $E$ and stable under $J$. These conclusions allow nonfaithful semilinear actions.

Normal means that every local ring is an integrally closed domain. H-projective means admitting a closed immersion into a finite-dimensional projective space over the target. A finite separable field extension is finite-dimensional with separable minimal polynomials. A finite Galois extension is a finite normal separable extension; normal for fields means that every irreducible polynomial over the smaller field with a root in the larger field splits there. For a group $G$ acting on a field $V$, $V^G$ is the subfield of elements fixed by every member of $G$. All fixed-field equalities below use the field embeddings induced by the displayed scheme maps. A primitive $\ell$th root of unity is an element of multiplicative order $\ell$. A finite morphism of integral curves is generically etale when it is etale over a dense open subset of its target. The notions used are [def-weil-field], [def-pc-integral-scheme], [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], [def-kun-projective], [def-sc-function-field], [def-pc-field-extension], [def-weil-pure-dimension], [def-weil-geometric-fibre], [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible], [def-fin-normalization-extension], [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], [def-weil-surjective-morphism], [def-pc-fibre-product], [def-weil-etale-morphism], [def-nagata-projective-space-base-change], [def-pc-genus], [def-weil-algebraic-closure].
statement_change.what: An affine cover may contain an empty open U_i. Its empty-source pencil has no generic affine coordinate in F, so x_i and the root list are then undefined. Require each U_i nonempty, as in the source: the opens are affine neighbourhoods of closed points. Deleting empty members changes none of the construction or applications.
